name: Sentinel
description: Sentinel watches Jellyfin playback sessions and explains, with evidence, why a specific transcode or playback problem happened — not just that it happened.
overview: Evidence-based root-cause diagnosis for Jellyfin playback problems

versions.changelog: Addresses live-server feedback on 0.1.6.2's notification/exception feature set, plus a logo fix and outbound webhook security. (1) Severity is now the five-level Info/Notice/Warning/Important/Critical scheme already drawn in Sentinel's own logo artwork, replacing the previous low/medium/high scheme everywhere (per-channel minimum-severity thresholds, Discord embed colors, notification dispatch) — Confidence maps 1:1 (Confirmed→Critical, VeryLikely→Important, Likely→Warning, Possible→Notice, Unknown→Info); existing per-channel MinSeverity config values reset to "info" (equivalent to the old "low"). (2) The "Mark as expected" per-incident button (added in 0.1.6.1, rescoped to per-user in 0.1.6.2) is replaced by a new Rule Policy settings panel: a fixed, admin-configurable Notify/Expected choice per diagnosis rule code, applied server-wide — matching direct feedback that a per-incident/per-user toggle still felt "per movie/show" rather than a real, general policy. The old IncidentException table is dropped (not migrated — the keying dimension changed from username to rule code) in favor of a new RulePolicy table; new GET Sentinel/rules and POST Sentinel/rules/{code}/policy endpoints back the panel. (3) Added an explanation of what "Minimum Severity" actually does. (4) The generic Webhook channel gains an optional shared secret, sent as an X-Sentinel-Secret header, so the receiving endpoint can verify a request actually came from this Sentinel instance. (5) Sentinel's logo was a dense square (1254x1254) mascot illustration with a fully transparent background; compared against a working reference plugin's logo (1920x1080, opaque dark background) this looked like a very plausible explanation for "displayed at the wrong size" in Jellyfin's plugin catalog card — reformatted (not redrawn) onto a matching 1920x1080 opaque dark canvas. Investigated but NOT code-changed, for lack of any actual defect found: plugin-update detection for a plugin outside any registered repository (Jellyfin's own GetAvailablePluginUpdates behavior, not a Sentinel bug), the installed-version display stuck at 0.1.5.0 despite 0.1.6.2 content (build.yaml has correctly read 0.1.6.2 since that release — looks like a stale local meta.json on that specific server), and which notification channels deliver reliably (reviewed the shared dispatch path again, no defect found; flagged for the admin to capture server logs next time it recurs). Deliberately deferred to a later release: Server-Health / media-codec-preference scanning (config target codec/resolution, periodic scan, notify-or-list-only) — the single largest new feature requested, scoped as its own release given its size. Verified: full local build and test suite (180/180 passing, 0 warnings/errors) against net10.0; all 7 locale files independently confirmed to carry an identical key set (91 keys); the ui-strings allowlist cross-checked against en.json to confirm no requested key is missing. NOT yet confirmed in a real browser against a live server by this session.

Fixes seven more issues found while actually using 0.1.6.1's notification channels on a live server. (1) "Send Test" required clicking the page's Save button first, or it silently tested the last-saved config instead of what was currently typed — the button now saves the current form state before sending. (2) A single click on "Send Test" sent several notifications at once — pageshow (Jellyfin's SPA navigation event) can fire more than once without a full page reload, and wiring the button's click listener unconditionally on every pageshow stacked a fresh listener on top of the old ones each time; wired exactly once now. (3) The Notification Channels settings (labels, buttons, status text) were still English-only regardless of the plugin's Language setting — 24 new UI strings added and localized across all 7 languages. (4) A transcode was only detected once playback stopped — Sentinel now diagnoses live during PlaybackProgress (verified against real Jellyfin source that PlaybackStopEventArgs is itself a PlaybackProgressEventArgs, so the exact same factory and rule engine run in both places), with a per-play-session guard so the same condition is never re-diagnosed or re-notified on a later tick or at the eventual stop. (5) Notifications only contained the explanation, not the recommendation for fixing it — both are now included. (6) "Mark as expected" was scoped to (rule code, user), which felt per-title since a single user's transcoding routinely trips different diagnosis codes on different videos — broadened to a single per-user exception (any rule, any media item), with a guarded migration that preserves any exceptions already marked under the old shape. (7) Discord notifications not arriving in production while Webhook/Email/Telegram worked: no code defect was found after a full review of all four channels and the config wiring — issue (1) above is a very plausible unifying explanation, since a Discord webhook URL typed but not explicitly saved before testing would have left production dispatch reading an empty/stale value; flagged for the admin to re-verify now that (1) is fixed. Also clarified for the admin: the plugin-update/restart-pending notification feature they believed was still missing already shipped in 0.1.6.0. Verified: full local build and test suite (177/177 passing, 0 warnings/errors) against net10.0, including two new tests proving live detection actually fires before any stop event and that the same condition is never double-diagnosed; all 7 locale files independently confirmed to carry an identical key set. NOT yet confirmed in a real browser against a live server by this session.

Fixes six issues found during the first real live-server test pass of 0.1.6.0. (1) The Language dropdown appeared empty when reopening the config page — root cause: the server can serialize the Language enum as its name (e.g. "De") rather than a number, which the dropdown only recognized numerically; now handles both. (2) Incident cards gave no visual hint that clicking expands them — added a chevron and "click for details" hint, localized in all 7 languages. (3) Added a free-text resolution-note field per incident, so an admin can record what actually fixed the problem for that user (new ResolutionNote column, POST Sentinel/incidents/{id}/note endpoint). (4) "Send test" on every notification channel failed with an uninformative generic message — a full review of the config save/load wiring and all four channel implementations found no code defect, so instead every channel now reports its real failure reason (HTTP status or exception message) via a new LastFailureReason surface, replacing the generic message with an actionable one. (5) The incident filter tabs (All/Active/Acknowledged/Resolved) rendered black text on a dark, semi-transparent background — native <button> elements don't inherit the page's text color by default, unlike <span>/<div>; fixed with an explicit color: inherit. (6) Added an exceptions feature: an admin can mark an incident's (rule code, username) combination as an accepted exception — e.g. a user who intentionally always transcodes via a GPU — via a new "Mark as expected" button; excepted incidents surface under a new "Expected" filter tab instead of "Active", and future notifications for that combination are suppressed (reversible via "Remove exception"). All six fixes were driven by real, specific live-server feedback, not speculative polish. Verified: full local build and test suite (174/174 passing, 0 warnings/errors) against the actual project TargetFramework (net10.0); all 7 locale files independently confirmed to carry an identical key set; the new dashboard JS's use of ApiClient.ajax (JSON POST body, and reading the failed-request Response object for the failure-reason JSON) was verified against Jellyfin's own jellyfin-apiclient-javascript source rather than assumed. NOT yet confirmed in a real browser against a live server by this session — that is the next step for the admin.

Adds plugin-update and restart-pending notifications — a new, user-requested feature not in the original master plan. Sentinel now checks hourly for available plugin updates (any installed plugin, not just itself) and notifies once per distinct plugin+version, deduplicated via a new NotifiedPluginUpdate table so the same update is never re-announced. Separately watches for a pending server restart and notifies exactly once on the transition into that state (never re-fires while already pending). These are deliberately two distinct notifications — an available update does not by itself imply a pending restart — verified against real Jellyfin v12.1 source (IInstallationManager.GetAvailablePluginUpdates, IApplicationHost.HasPendingRestartChanged) rather than assumed. Also: a holistic security review across the full plugin source found zero Critical/High/Medium/Low findings — SQL injection, credential handling, dashboard XSS, and controller authorization were all confirmed clean; one Informational note (outbound webhook/SMTP destinations have no private-IP-range validation) was reviewed and judged a deliberately accepted non-issue given this plugin's real threat model. This release marks completion of the originally-requested MVP scope (localization, Incident Engine, Notification Delivery, modern dashboard) plus every explicitly-requested addition (Series-Episode display, per-incident user tracking, admin sidebar entry, and this plugin-update/restart feature).

Real dashboard visual overhaul, in direct response to live-server feedback that the previous release's UI "still doesn't look good". The Notification Channels settings section (added in 0.1.5.2) was completely unstyled — a long list of plain stacked form fields sitting above the actual incident dashboard, so it was the first thing visible on page load instead of Sentinel's real content. Now: the settings collapse into a closed-by-default accordion so incidents are the first thing visible; each of the four channels (Webhook/Discord/Telegram/Email) gets its own card in a responsive grid with brand-accurate accent colors; test-send results are color-coded (green success / red failure) instead of plain text. Every existing field id and API interaction is unchanged — pure structural/CSS restructuring, reviewed with explicit focus on confirming none of the 18 settings-field ids or 4 channel-name strings drifted during the rewrite. Still not verified in a real browser by this session (no reachable instance here) — this release exists specifically so the user can judge the actual result themselves on their own server.

Adds Notification Delivery — Webhook, Discord, Telegram, and Email (via MailKit) channels, a severity mapping (diagnosis confidence to low/medium/high), and a dedup-aware dispatcher that notifies exactly once per new-or-reopened Incident (never per raw diagnosis or per plain occurrence-count increment). Dashboard gains a per-channel config section (enable, destination/credential fields, minimum-severity threshold, and a mandatory "Send test" button per channel). Also adds: tracking and display of which Jellyfin user hit each diagnosis/incident (never part of the Incident dedup fingerprint, to avoid fragmenting incidents on shared household devices/profiles); Sentinel's own entry in the server admin sidebar under Plugins; an incident filter/count tab bar (All/Active/Acknowledged/Resolved) and a small visual polish pass on the dashboard. One security-relevant fix applied before release: the Email channel initially used SecureSocketOptions.Auto, which can silently fall back to an unencrypted SMTP connection if the server doesn't advertise STARTTLS — changed to StartTls/SslOnConnect, which fail the connection outright instead of downgrading, so SMTP credentials can never be sent in cleartext. Notification Delivery is NOT yet wired to the plugin-update/restart-pending feature (still planned, not in this release) and has not been verified against real Discord/Telegram/Email/webhook endpoints — that needs the admin's own credentials and is tracked as a post-release verification step. Verified by a fresh-subagent review after every task (spec compliance + code quality, including independent re-runs of the full test suite, independent re-derivation of MailKit's exact publish-output dependency list, and independent verification of the TLS-downgrade fix); one real, non-blocking test-coverage gap (the dispatcher's channel-wiring logic) found by a task reviewer was fixed before this release, not left open.

Adds full localization (English, German, Spanish, French, Swedish, Danish, Polish) — a per-plugin Language setting, and every diagnosis explanation/recommendation plus every dashboard UI string is now translated at serve time via a new GET Sentinel/ui-strings endpoint. Fixes the dashboard's media display to show "Series - Episode Name" for TV episodes instead of just the episode name. Adds the Incident Engine: diagnoses sharing the same rule code, media item, client, and device are now deduplicated into a single Incident (via a partial unique SQLite index on that fingerprint) instead of alerting once per raw diagnosis; a resolved incident that recurs reopens instead of duplicating; new GET/POST Sentinel/incidents endpoints (list, acknowledge, resolve). The dashboard is rewritten from a plain diagnosis table into a card-based Incident view with status badges, occurrence counts, and working Acknowledge/Resolve buttons, plus a language selector wired to the new setting. Notification Delivery (Webhook/Discord/Telegram/Email), the plugin-update/restart-pending notification feature, and a dedicated security review are NOT yet in this release — tracked for a following one. Verified by a fresh-subagent review after every task (spec compliance + code quality, including independent re-runs of the full test suite and independent JSON-validity checks on all 7 locale files); not yet confirmed against a real Jellyfin server for any of this release's features.

Adds five new diagnosis rules covering external audio tracks, HDR/dynamic-range mismatches, audio channel downmixing, bitrate-only transcodes, and resolution-only transcodes — including the exact real-world case confirmed on a live server in 0.1.4.0 (an AV1 transcode with only an audio-channel-downmix reason, previously unrecognized). Also wires up the previously dormant Known Core Issues table into the API and dashboard, surfaced as a distinct "Known Jellyfin Bug" note. Verified by three rounds of independent review; each rule's PlayMethod == Transcode gate and mutual exclusivity with stronger, more specific diagnoses is covered by a dedicated regression test, verified RED/GREEN by temporarily removing every gate and confirming each one is independently caught. Not yet confirmed against a real server for these specific new rules.

Fixes a data-integrity bug confirmed on a real server running 0.1.3.0: a session with a verified, active ffmpeg transcode (video re-encoded, audio downmixed — confirmed via the server's own transcode log) still produced a PlaybackEvent row with PlayMethod = DirectPlay next to a correctly non-zero TranscodeReasons, silently suppressing the diagnosis despite the reasons having been captured correctly. PlaybackEventFactory now forces PlayMethod to Transcode when TranscodeReasons is non-default and PlayMethod resolved to DirectPlay or null (DirectStream/remux sessions are correctly left alone, since they legitimately carry non-zero TranscodeReasons too — a broader first version of this fix was caught and narrowed during review before release). Verified by two rounds of independent review plus a regression test reproducing the exact real-world contradiction; not yet re-confirmed against a real server for this specific fix.

Fixes a bug affecting every previous version: Jellyfin always clears the play method and transcode-reason data on a session before firing the event this plugin used to read them from, so PlaybackEvent rows were recorded with an empty play method and zero transcode reasons regardless of whether a transcode actually happened — confirmed live with a real bitrate-driven transcode that produced a blank database row despite Jellyfin's own dashboard showing an active transcode with a specific reason. Sentinel now also listens to playback-progress events (while that data is still live) and caches it per playback, including a fallback for Jellyfin's own idle-timeout stop path, which never supplies the identifier this plugin would otherwise key on. Verified by three rounds of independent review plus targeted regression tests reproducing the exact real-world event sequence; not yet re-confirmed against a real server for this specific fix.

Adds a minimal read-only dashboard to the plugin's configuration page: recent diagnoses (media, client/device, confidence, explanation) with click-to-expand evidence, backed by a new admin-only API endpoint. Verified by code inspection, two independent review rounds, and a clean local build/test run; not yet independently confirmed against a real server for this specific feature.

Fixes a confirmed bug in 0.1.0.0: installing on a real Jellyfin server resulted in status 'Malfunctioned' because of native SQLite library loading (see build.yaml changelog for the full root cause). Confirmed loading and running correctly on a real Jellyfin 12.1 server. 0.1.0.0 is removed from this list since it is confirmed broken.
